title: proactive-saturation-prober-with-exponential-backoff-for-continuous-batcher
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Adds a proactive saturation prober and per-queue exponential backoff to reduce starvation and tail latency for continuous batching. Backwards-compatible config knobs and rollout plan included.
description: Context and motivation: Continuous batcher instances occasionally experience transient queue saturation when traffic fan-in spikes or when KV cache warmups produce long requests. Existing heuristics are reactive (drop/evict after threshold) and occasionally lead to unfairness or short-term starvation for lower-priority queues. This PR implements a proactive saturation prober that periodically probes queue headroom and triggers graded backoff and eviction policies before hard saturation occurs. Design summary: 1) lightweight prober thread per batcher group that issues controlled, non-user requests (probes) with low token cost to measure effective slot availability and observed dispatch latency; 2) per-queue saturation score computed from probe RTT, pending-slot-duration, and recent eviction counts; 3) exponential backoff factor applied to a queue's admission rate when saturation score exceeds thresholds, with jitter to avoid synchronized pacing; 4) a soft-eviction escalation path when backoff is insufficient for a sustained window; 5) integration with KV cache pinning heuristics so pinned KV-heavy requests get a grace allowance while still preventing starvation. Implementation details: - runtime/batcher/proactive_prober.go: new prober implementation (350 LOC) with pluggable sampler and metrics hooks. - runtime/batcher/prober_config.go: Tunable config struct with sensible defaults and dynamic refresh from operator flags. - runtime/batcher/prober_test.go: Unit tests for scoring, jitter, and backoff algebra. - runtime/batcher/scheduler_integration.go: Hooks that convert saturation score to admission control decisions; minimal changes to existing scheduler code path. - bench/continuous_batcher/prober_bench.yml: Bench harness to replay production trace (anon) and measure p50/p99. - docs/internal/batcher-prober.md: Operator docs and rollout guidance (canary percent, expected signals). Safety and compatibility: The prober defaults to disabled in cluster config; enabling requires opt-in via a runtime flag so this can be rolled out progressively. All control paths have fallbacks to the current admission logic. Performance results (canary run, 3% traffic, 4 runs): - p50 generation latency: +2% (noise) - p95 generation latency: -6% - p99 generation latency: -18% - request success rate: unchanged - CPU overhead on batcher pods: +4% typical (prober worker) Observability: New metrics exported with prefix batcher.prober.*: probe_rtt_ms, probe_success_ratio, queue_saturation_score, queue_backoff_factor. Logs include a level info line when a queue transitions into backoff and a level warn when soft-eviction is applied. Tests and CI: Unit tests added and integration bench validates behavior against a baseline harness. CI: lint, go-test, bench-run (smoke) passed; one flaky bench run requeued and passed on re-run. Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Enable on small percentage of fleet (3%) for 24h; monitor queue_saturation_score and p99 latency. 3) Ramp to 25% then 100% if stable. 4) If soft-evictions increase >2x baseline or p99 regresses >10% revert flag. Checklist: - [x] Core prober implementation and tests - [x] Scheduler integration and admission control mapping - [x] Bench harness + perf numbers - [x] Docs and operator guidance - [x] Feature-flag gating - [x] Rollout plan and dashboards (Grafana panels added) Follow-ups: - Evaluate combining prober signal with KV cache affinity scoring to reduce false positives for large pinned KV requests - Auto-tune backoff thresholds via RL-style controller in a later PR - Expand bench scenarios to include cross-region traffic spikes

notes: This PR was intentionally conservative: feature flag off by default, limited rollout, and clear observability hooks. The improvement on p99 during canary justified enabling the flag for wider audience in the next sprint.
